title: Lemon Mascarpone French Toast with Strawberries
changes_from_base: The custard is sweetened with maple syrup, and each plate gets a whipped lemon mascarpone cream and lemony macerated strawberries with toasted nuts instead of cinnamon sugar.
summary: Fluffy brioche fried until golden and topped with a tangy lemon mascarpone cream, sweet strawberries and toasted nuts.
equipment: wire rack set in a rimmed baking tray

ingredients.item: strawberries, hulled and quartered (eighths if large)
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
slices brioche or challah, 2.5 cm thick (about 450 g)
flaked almonds (or pistachios or hazelnuts), toasted

steps.title: Macerate
steps.text: Stir 450 g quartered strawberries with 3 tbsp caster sugar, 1 tsp lemon zest, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tsp vanilla and ⅛ tsp salt, then leave at room temperature for 30 min, stirring once.

steps.title: Whip
steps.text: Whisk 225 g mascarpone with 60 g yoghurt, 3 tbsp maple syrup, 1 tbsp lemon zest, 1 tbsp lemon juice and ⅛ tsp salt until smooth, then chill.

steps.title: Whisk custard
steps.text: Beat 3 eggs with 240 ml milk, 2 tbsp maple syrup, 28 g melted butter, 1 tsp vanilla, ¼ tsp cinnamon and ¼ tsp salt in a shallow dish.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Dip each of the 8 brioche or challah slices into the custard for 30 s per side, then drain on a wire rack for 1 min.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Melt half of the 42 g butter in a large non-stick pan over medium-low heat and cook 4 slices until deep golden, 3-4 min per side, lowering the heat if they colour too fast.

steps.title: Keep warm
steps.text: Cover the cooked slices with foil while melting the remaining butter and frying the last 4 slices.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Plate 2 slices per person topped with the lemon cream, macerated strawberries and their juice, and 25 g toasted flaked almonds.

tips: Press the centre of a slice gently; it's ready when it springs back and no longer feels wet.
Lower the heat if the outside browns before the inside is cooked through.
Let the strawberries sit the full 30 minutes so their juices form a light syrup.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best eaten fresh and warm; keep any leftover lemon cream covered in the fridge for a day and the cooked toast loosely covered for a few hours. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
